Notes: James I conquered the city in 1229 and did not attack the Jewish community; Jews received properties incl. the area next to the royal palace (Almudaina). Earliest firmly city-specific documented presence (Year Established)
About 1271 the community of Palma paid an annual tax of 5000 solidos; organized community, no headcount
About 1290 the Jews of Palma were assigned a special walled ghetto with gates; earlier (Moorish period) Jews lived in the Almudayna
2000 Jews in Mallorca in 1297 - ISLAND-WIDE figure, not Palma alone (Bernat i Roca citing Rossello Vaquer)
Around 1300 James II ordered the Jews to move to a new quarter (the Call Major)
In 1314 King Sancho confiscated the synagogue and converted it into the Church of Santa Fe
Arrival of 60 families from France (after the 1311 French expulsion) contributed to growth of the call; immigrant subset (~300 persons), not total population
Call of Ciutat de Mallorca: 495 morabati taxpayers (hearths); author's estimate 1980-2475 (coef. 4-5), 2227 at coef. 4.5; 9.17% of city. Hypothetical fiscal-based estimate
In 1331 James III permitted a new plain synagogue; there were also two smaller synagogues
Call of Ciutat de Mallorca: 371 morabati taxpayers; estimate 1484-1855 (coef. 4-5), 1669 at 4.5; author attributes the drop to fiscal rather than demographic causes
289 Jewish debtors of the aljama for the cabecatge tax in 1339 - taxpayer subset, not total population
Call of Ciutat de Mallorca: 333 morabati taxpayers; estimate 1332-1665 (coef. 4-5), 1498 at 4.5
Call of Ciutat de Mallorca: 465 morabati taxpayers; estimate 1860-2325 (coef. 4-5), 2092 at 4.5
Monedatge of 1350 lists 735 heads of household in the call; at 4-5 persons per hearth 2940-3675 Jews, mean 3307; about 20% of the city's population
About three thousand Jews (c.15% of the city's population) during the 14th-century heyday; source gives only the century, midpoint 1350 used
2 Aug 1391: 300 Jews killed in Palma; many fled by ship to North Africa; all who remained accepted baptism (death toll, not population)
Riots in Palma broke out on 10 July 1391; mob broke down the gates of the Jewish quarter and massacred scores of Jews

24 Aug 1391 (per this source): about 300 Jews murdered and 800 saved themselves in the royal castle; rest baptized (event counts). Source also says Mallorca had more than 1000 Jewish families at its height (island-wide, undated)
About 300 killed in the assault on the call; about 150 Jews converted to Christianity for the first time (event counts)
In 1394 the Jewish population increased with the arrival of 150 Portuguese Jews (immigrant subset)

Article states that in 1435 Palma de Mallorca's Jewish community included some 4000 people (popular news source; conflicts with scholarly accounts of a shrunken community) [Review fix: Population 4000 moved to Notes - popular news source contradicting the documented end of the community in 1435]
1435: after a blood-libel the community ceased to exist - 200 persons were converted and the remainder fled (conversion count, not population)
1435 ritual-murder accusation: several hundred Jews baptized; this put an end to the Jewish community of Palma and the synagogue was turned into a church (documented end of the community)
Inquisition edict of grace: 680 conversos reconciled - these were baptized crypto-Jews, not a Jewish population count
From 1672 (trials to 1679) 218 chuetas (crypto-Jewish conversos) condemned to fines and prison
In 1691, 37 people were burned in a Palma square because they were Jewish (conversos; plaque unveiled 2018)

Until the 20th century about 400 Chueta families (Catholic descendants of converts) lived as a closed society in the Sagell/Plateria area - not a Jewish population; 'until the 20th century' dated as 1900
British expats revived Jewish life in Palma in 1971; city has a synagogue, Jewish museum and resident rabbi
Community reborn at the turn of the 1970s and officially recognised at a ceremony on its premises in 1987; synagogue at Monsenyor Palmer 3
Chuetas of Majorca (descendants of converts; close to 15000) recognized as Jewish by a Bnei Brak rabbinical court; not a Jewish population count
Palma's Jewish community includes 200 to 250 people (midpoint used) plus 'guests' during the year; one active synagogue; article dated 29 Sep 2015
Island of Mallorca has a small active Jewish community of about 100 members plus expats (island-level, centered in Palma); 50th anniversary of 1971 founding
More than 200 converts to Judaism in the Balearic Islands meet at the Palma synagogue (regional subset)
